overview: Umbrella review of systematic reviews of point-of-order imaging decision support, with a focus on low back pain, AMSTAR 2 appraisal, an overlap matrix and a narrative synthesis for a non-clinical board.
population: Systematic reviews of adults for whom imaging was ordered in primary care or emergency departments, with a low back pain subset.
exposure: Electronic decision support at the point of ordering imaging, compared with no decision support or usual vetting.
procedures: Search four databases and a registry of review protocols from 2010; two reviewers screen and extract; AMSTAR 2 appraisal by two reviewers; citation matrix with corrected covered area; for each outcome, the most recent review with the highest AMSTAR 2 rating is primary; conflicts resolved by returning to the primary studies they share.

outcomes.name: Inappropriate imaging orders
outcomes.measure: Relative change in the proportion of orders judged inappropriate, as reported by the selected review

outcomes.name: Pain and function
outcomes.measure: Patient-reported pain and function at the latest reported time point
outcomes.why: Checks that fewer images do not harm patients.

outcomes.name: Override of alerts
outcomes.why: Decides alert design in the specification.

outcomes.name: Evidence overlap
outcomes.measure: Corrected covered area across included reviews

feasibility: Ten information specialist days and two part-time reviewers until March 2027.

biasFlags.label: Low-quality reviews
biasFlags.note: Most reviews are critically low on AMSTAR 2; primary review selection rules fixed in advance.

parsimony.simplestPath: One primary outcome, one review per outcome, overlap reported.

summary: Umbrella review protocol with one primary outcome and overlap handling.
